# ASN.1 DER differential tests

These tests compare our verified ASN.1 DER parser with three unverified
implementations:

* [asn1tools](https://github.com/eerimoq/asn1tools) (Python), with its `der` codec;
* [rasn](https://github.com/librasn/rasn) (Rust), with types generated by
  [rasn-compiler](https://github.com/librasn/compiler);
* [asn1-rs](https://github.com/rusticata/asn1-rs) (Rust), with types written by
  hand using its derive macros, since it has no ASN.1 compiler.

They run as part of `make -C src/ASN1 test`, and so as part of the toplevel
`make test`.

## Principles

* Each vector's expected verdict (`accept` or `reject`) comes from X.690 or
  X.680, and the vector cites the clause. It is never copied from our parser's
  output.
* A vector runs on an implementation only if every feature it is tagged with
  is `supported` or `partial` in that implementation's `capabilities/*.json`.
  DER strictness is not a capability: all three implementations claim to
  decode DER.
* Our parser must agree with every expected verdict. Any other disagreement
  is a *discrepancy*. Each discrepancy must be triaged (classified) in
  `triage/known.json`, so `make test` only fails on regressions.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `schemas/*.asn` | ASN.1 modules, the input for asn1tools and rasn-compiler |
| `../ASN1.DiffTest.*.fst` | F\* translations of the schemas |
| `../ASN1.DiffTest.fst` | name-based dispatch (`"Module.Type"`), extracted with the parser |
| `features.json` | the catalog of feature tags |
| `vectors/*.json` | test vectors: `id`, `type`, `hex`, `expect`, `clause`, `features`, optional `mutation`, `notes` |
| `capabilities/<impl>.json` | per-implementation feature support, with the evidence for it |
| `triage/known.json` | triaged discrepancies: `impl`, `id`, `got`, `class`, `clause`, `rationale`, `upstream` |
| `harness/asn1tools/` | Python runner; `requirements.txt` pins the version |
| `harness/rust/` | Cargo workspace (`rasn-runner`, `asn1rs-runner`); `Cargo.lock` pins the versions |
| `report.py` | manifest assembly, report and gating |
| `out/` | generated: `manifest.json`, `<impl>.jsonl` results, `report.md` |

Every runner shares one command line, `RUNNER MANIFEST RESULTS`. It writes one
JSON object per vector:

```json
{"id": ..., "impl": ..., "verdict": "accept|reject|unsupported|error", "consumed": ...}
```

The verdict is `accept` only if decoding succeeds *and* consumes the whole
input.

## Usage

```sh
make -C src/ASN1/difftest            # same as `check`
make -C src/ASN1/difftest rebaseline
make -C src/ASN1/difftest clean
```

* `check` runs every enabled implementation, then gates. It fails if:
  1. our verdict differs from the expected verdict;
  2. a discrepancy is new, or still `untriaged`;
  3. a baseline entry no longer occurs (stale).

  The full report is written to `out/report.md`.
* `rebaseline` rewrites `triage/known.json` from the current results:
  * stale entries are dropped;
  * existing classifications are kept;
  * new discrepancies are added as `untriaged`. Classify them before
    committing.
* `clean` removes `out/`, `.venv/` and the Rust `target/`.

Toolchains:

* The `.venv` is created on first use, as in `share/everparse/tests/cbor`.
* The Rust runners use the ambient `cargo`, as in `src/cbor/tests_rust`.
* The first run needs network access to download from PyPI and crates.io.

Opt-outs:

* `ASN1_DIFFTEST_PY=0` skips asn1tools.
* `ASN1_DIFFTEST_RUST=0` skips rasn and asn1-rs.
* Without `cargo` on `PATH`, the Rust runners are skipped with a warning.

Implementations that were not run are not gated.

## Triage classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `harness` | runner or schema-translation bug (should be fixed, not recorded) |
| `manifest` | wrong expected verdict (should be fixed, not recorded) |
| `policy` | ours is deliberately stricter than X.690 |
| `ambiguity` | X.690 is unclear |
| `documented-leniency` | leniency documented by the implementation |
| `bug-asn1tools`, `bug-rasn`, `bug-asn1-rs` | implementation bug, with evidence in `rationale` |

A majority vote among the implementations is a hint, never a verdict.

## Adding a test

1. Add or extend a module in `schemas/`.
2. Translate it to F\* in `../ASN1.DiffTest.<Module>.fst`, and add each type
   to the dispatch in `../ASN1.DiffTest.fst`.
3. Add each type to the dispatch in `harness/rust/rasn-runner/src/main.rs`,
   and translate it by hand in `harness/rust/asn1rs-runner/src/main.rs`.
4. Add vectors to `vectors/`, tagged with features from `features.json`.
5. Run `make -C src/ASN1 test`, then triage any new discrepancies.
